note: Layout Disable hides layout plugins from every layout picker. Code-grounded facts: disabled layouts are stored in config object layout_disable.settings under key disabled_layouts (associative list keyed by layout plugin id); hook_layout_alter() removes them via array_diff_key from the core layout plugin manager (plugin.manager.core.layout); form route 'layout_disable' at /admin/config/user-interface/layout-disable, permission 'access layout_disable'; layout_onecol and layout_builder_blank are core-required and cannot be disabled; a cache clear of the layout plugin manager is required for changes to show (the form does it). Medium cases install known state (a specific layout disabled) discoverable via config or the running plugin manager. Hard cases build real state verified against BOTH the config and the layout plugin manager: disable a layout, and re-enable an already-disabled layout.

evals.prompt: Using the Layout Disable module on Drupal 11, how do you make a layout unavailable, and where/how is that stored so it disappears from Layout Builder's layout picker?
evals.expected_output: Tick the layout on the Disable layouts form; the selected layout plugin ids are saved to config layout_disable.settings under disabled_layouts (keyed by layout id). layout_disable_layout_alter() (hook_layout_alter) then removes those ids from the layout definitions with array_diff_key, so they no longer appear in any layout picker.

evals.prompt: In the Layout Disable module, at which admin path is the disable-layouts form and which permission controls access to it?
evals.expected_output: The form is at /admin/config/user-interface/layout-disable (route 'layout_disable') and requires the 'access layout_disable' permission.

evals.prompt: Which layouts can NOT be disabled with the Layout Disable module, and why?
evals.expected_output: layout_onecol and layout_builder_blank are core-required and are excluded from the form, so they cannot be disabled.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, exactly one layout has been disabled with the Layout Disable module. Inspect the live configuration and give the machine name (plugin id) of the disabled layout.
evals.expected_output: layout_twocol_bricks is disabled: it is listed in layout_disable.settings:disabled_layouts (readable via `drush cget layout_disable.settings disabled_layouts`) and is absent from the core layout plugin manager's definitions.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, one of the three-column section layouts is no longer available in the layout picker because it was disabled with the Layout Disable module. Inspect the running layout plugin list (or the module's configuration) and name the disabled layout's plugin id.
evals.expected_output: layout_threecol_25_50_25 has been disabled: it appears in layout_disable.settings:disabled_layouts and the layout plugin manager (plugin.manager.core.layout) no longer has a definition for it.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the Layout Disable module to disable the four-column section layout (layout_fourcol_section) so it no longer appears in any layout picker. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: layout_fourcol_section is added to layout_disable.settings:disabled_layouts (via the form or config) and, after the layout plugin cache is cleared, the core layout plugin manager no longer has a definition for it.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the two-column layout (layout_twocol) has been disabled with the Layout Disable module and editors can no longer choose it. Re-enable it so it is available again. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: layout_twocol is removed from layout_disable.settings:disabled_layouts (uncheck it on the form, or clear the key) and, after clearing the layout plugin cache, the layout plugin manager has a definition for layout_twocol again.
